lem-classifying-maps-are-natural-under-g:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $f:(X,x_0)\to(Y,y_0)$ be a based map of path-connected CW
complexes, let $G=\pi_1(X,x_0)$ and $H=\pi_1(Y,y_0)$, and put
$\phi=f_*:G\to H$. Let $c_X:X\to BG$ and $c_Y:Y\to BH$ be based classifying
maps inducing the identity on the identified fundamental groups. There is a
based map $B\phi:BG\to BH$ inducing $\phi$, and
$$
B\phi\circ c_X\simeq c_Y\circ f
$$
by a based homotopy. Consequently the induced maps on singular homology commute.
lem-h2-classifying-map-is-surjective:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $X$ be a path-connected CW complex and let $G=\pi_1(X,x_0)$.
For any based classifying map $c:X\to BG$ inducing the identity on fundamental
groups, the induced homomorphism
$$
c_*:H_2(X;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H_2(BG;\mathbb Z)=H_2(G;\mathbb Z)
$$
is surjective.
lem-regular-link-diagram-admits-normaliz:
## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a
nonempty labeled smooth link $L\subset\mathbb R^3$, and assume every component
has at least one underpassing point. Then $L$ is ambient isotopic through links
with the same projection and crossing data to a smooth height realization
$$
\widehat L=\{(\gamma_i(s),\widehat\eta_i(s)):s\in S^1,\ 1\le i\le r\}
\subset\mathbb R^2\times[-1,0]
$$
such that $\widehat\eta_i(s)=-1$ exactly at the underpassing parameters on
component $i$ and $\widehat\eta_i(s)>-1$ at every other parameter.
lem-simply-connected-hypersurface-comple:
## Statement

Let $M$ be a connected smooth $3$-manifold without boundary, and let $S\subset M$
be a nonempty closed connected smooth embedded surface with
$\pi_1(S)=1$. Suppose there is an open neighborhood $N$ of $S$ such that
$N$ is path-connected and simply connected, and $N\setminus S$ has exactly two
path-connected simply connected components $N_-$ and $N_+$. Suppose also that
$M\setminus S$ is path-connected and contains an embedded compact arc
$\nu$ joining $N_-$ to $N_+$, with an open tubular neighborhood $T$ such that
$T\cap N$ consists of exactly two disjoint open $3$-balls, one in each side
component. Then
$$
\pi_1(M)\cong \pi_1(M\setminus S)*\mathbb Z.
$$
The cyclic factor is represented by a loop that joins the two sides of $N$ and
returns between them through $M\setminus S$.
thm-homological-lhs-spectral-sequence-fo:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every short exact sequence of discrete groups
$$
1\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow 1,
$$
the homological Serre spectral sequence of the induced map of classifying spaces
has
$$
E^2_{p,q}\cong H_p\!\left(Q;H_q(N;\mathbb Z)\right)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
H_{p+q}(G;\mathbb Z).
$$
Here $H_p(Q;M)$ denotes homology of $BQ$ with the local coefficient system
determined by the left $Q$-module $M$, and group homology uses the bar
classifying spaces. The coefficient group $H_q(N;\mathbb Z)$ has the $Q$-action
induced by conjugation by lifts in $G$, and convergence is strong with the
finite Serre filtration in each total degree.
thm-five-term-homology-sequence-for-grou:
## Statement

Assume AC. For every group extension
$$
1\longrightarrow N\longrightarrow G\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow 1,
$$
the maps induced by inclusion, quotient, and transgression form an exact sequence
$$
H_2(G;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H_2(Q;\mathbb Z)
\longrightarrow N/[G,N]\longrightarrow H_1(G;\mathbb Z)
\longrightarrow H_1(Q;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow 0.
$$
Here $[G,N]$ is the normal subgroup generated by the commutators
$gng^{-1}n^{-1}$ with $g\in G$ and $n\in N$.
thm-stallings-integral-lower-central-iso:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\phi:A\to B$ be a group homomorphism inducing an isomorphism
$H_1(A;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(B;\mathbb Z)$ and an epimorphism
$H_2(A;\mathbb Z)\to H_2(B;\mathbb Z)$. For a group $X$, define
$\Gamma_1X=X$ and $\Gamma_{n+1}X=[X,\Gamma_nX]$. Then for every finite
$n\ge1$, the induced homomorphism
$$
A/\Gamma_nA\longrightarrow B/\Gamma_nB
$$
is an isomorphism.
def-lower-central-series-and-magnus-expa:
## Definition

For any group $G$, define its lower-central series by $\Gamma_1G=G$ and
$\Gamma_{q+1}G=[G,\Gamma_qG]$, where $[G,H]$ is the subgroup generated by
$ghg^{-1}h^{-1}$ for $g\in G$ and $h\in H$. For $r\ge1$, let
$F_r=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_r\rangle$ be the free group on the formal meridian
symbols $x_i$, with the free-group convention of its stated generators.

Let $\mathcal A_r=\mathbb Z\langle\!\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r\rangle\!\rangle$
be the ring of formal integer sums $\sum_w a_wX_w$ over all finite words $w$
in the letters $X_i$, with multiplication given by concatenation of words.
This is the degree-complete ring for the word-length filtration; a series with
invertible constant coefficient is a unit, with inverse determined recursively
degree by degree.
Filter it by total degree (word length), and let $\mathfrak m$ be the ideal of
series with zero constant term.
The Magnus expansion is the group homomorphism
$$
E:F_r\longrightarrow
\mathbb Z\langle\!\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r\rangle\!\rangle^\times,
\qquad E(x_i)=1+X_i.
$$
It sends $x_i^{-1}$ to $(1+X_i)^{-1}=\sum_{k\ge0}(-1)^kX_i^k$. For an
integer $d\ge0$, calculations through degree $d$ use the truncated ring
$R_d=\mathbb Z\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r\rangle/\mathfrak m^{d+1}$. As a
$\mathbb Z$-module it has the finite monomial basis of words of length at most
$d$. In $R_d$, the inverse of $1+A$ for $A\in\mathfrak m$ is the finite sum
$1-A+A^2-\cdots+(-A)^d$.

For a based string link, $x_1,\ldots,x_r$ may be used as formal symbols
corresponding to the positive bottom-end meridians. No freeness or
lower-central quotient isomorphism is asserted here; those properties require
separate proofs.
lem-link-diagram-upper-region-free-merid:
## Statement

Assume countable choice.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a nonempty labeled link with
$n\geq1$ crossings. Fix a smooth height realization
$L_D=\{(\gamma(s),\eta(s))\}\subset\mathbb R^2\times[-1,0]$ such that
$\eta(s)=-1$ exactly at the $n$ underpassing points and $\eta(s)>-1$
elsewhere, and assume each component has at least one underpassing point. Put
$$M=(\mathbb R^2\times(-1,\infty))\setminus L_D.$$
Cut every component parameter circle at its underpassing points; the resulting
$n$ open intervals are the strands. For each strand interval $I_j$, its
vertical sheet is
$$D_j=\{(\gamma(s),z):s\in I_j,\ -1<z<\eta(s)\}\subset M.$$
Set $Z=M\setminus\bigcup_{j=1}^nD_j$. Choose a common basepoint in $Z$, and
for each strand choose a positive meridian circle meeting only its own sheet
once, with its access path in $Z$. Then $\pi_1(M)$ is free on these based
positive meridians $x_1,\ldots,x_n$. The inclusion $M\hookrightarrow A_L$
also induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups.
lem-link-nilpotent-quotient-generated-by:
## Statement

Let $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_r$ be a nonempty labeled oriented link in $S^3$,
let $G=\pi_1(E_L)$, and choose one based positive meridian $m_i\in G$ for each
component. For every integer $q\geq1$, the homomorphism from the free group
$F_r=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_r\rangle$ defined by $x_i\mapsto m_i$ induces a
surjection
$$F_r\longrightarrow G/\Gamma_qG.$$
lem-magnus-commutator-degree-and-truncat:
## Statement

Let $F_r$ be the free group and $E$ the Magnus expansion from the preceding
definition, with augmentation ideal $\mathfrak m$. If
$u\in\Gamma_pF_r$ and $v\in\Gamma_qF_r$ for $p,q\ge1$, then
$$
E([u,v])\in 1+\mathfrak m^{p+q}.
$$
Consequently $E(\Gamma_qF_r)\subseteq1+\mathfrak m^q$ for every $q\ge1$.
In particular, reduction of $E$ modulo $\mathfrak m^{d+1}$ factors through
$F_r/\Gamma_{d+1}F_r$ and its coefficients through degree $d$ are independent
of the representative word.
lem-magnus-conjugation-coefficients-use-:
## Statement

Let $F_r$ be the free group with Magnus expansion $E$, let $u,\lambda\in F_r$,
and let $w$ be a nonempty word of length $m$. The coefficient of $X_w$ in
$E(u^{-1}\lambda u)-E(\lambda)$ is an integer linear combination of
coefficients of $E(\lambda)$ on proper contiguous subwords of $w$. Thus, when
$w$ is the prefix of a Milnor index $I=(w,j)$, conjugating the longitude can
change its degree-$m$ coefficient only by an integer combination of
coefficients indexed by proper subsequences of $I$.
thm-string-link-nilpotent-peripheral-ide:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\tau$ be an $r$-component based string link with $r\geq1$,
exterior $X_\tau$, and endpoint punctured disks $P_-,P_+$. Use compatible jointly transported stem accesses for the positive
endpoint meridians to identify $\pi_1(P_-)$ and $\pi_1(P_+)$ with the free
group $F_r=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_r\rangle$, and let
$\iota_\pm:\pi_1(P_\pm)\to\pi_1(X_\tau)$ be the based end homomorphisms,
including the chosen top connecting path. For every integer $q\geq1$, each
induced map
$$\iota_{\pm,q}:F_r/\Gamma_qF_r\longrightarrow \pi_1(X_\tau)/\Gamma_q\pi_1(X_\tau)$$
is an isomorphism. Their composite
$\iota_{-,q}^{-1}\iota_{+,q}$ is the based nilpotent comparison of the labeled
top and bottom peripheral systems.

Arbitrary independently based positive endpoint meridians are retained as well: the map from the free symbol group $F_r$ sending $x_i$ to that chosen meridian need not identify the full fundamental group, but its composites with the end maps still induce the displayed isomorphisms on every finite lower-central quotient. Their inverse/composite is the comparison for those exact choices, and the conjugating access differences are part of the data.
def-milnor-integer-and-residue-invariant:
## Definition

Assume AC for the string-link quotient branch. Use the closed-link residue
definition one finite maximum index length at a time, so its based word-lift
data are finite.

Let $\tau$ be a based $r$-component string link with bottom meridian symbol group
$F_r=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_r\rangle$, exterior group $G=\pi_1(X_\tau)$, and
based string-link longitudes $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r$. With compatible stem accesses this free group identifies the full endpoint fundamental group. For arbitrary independently based meridians, use instead its meridian map on each finite nilpotent quotient, which is still an isomorphism by the end-identification theorem; no full-group free-basis assertion is made. Longitudes retain their specified parallel and access data. For a multi-index
$I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k,j)$ with $k\geq1$ and each index in $\{1,\ldots,r\}$,
let $w_{j,k}\in F_r/\Gamma_{k+1}F_r$ be the unique class whose image under
the bottom-end nilpotent isomorphism is the class of $\lambda_j$ in
$G/\Gamma_{k+1}G$. Define the integer coefficient
$$\mu_\tau(I)=[X_{i_1}\cdots X_{i_k}]\,E(w_{j,k})\in\mathbb Z,$$
where the bracket means the coefficient of that word in the finite Magnus
expansion through degree $k$. The commutator-degree lemma makes this coefficient
independent of the representative of $w_{j,k}$.

For a closed labeled link $L$, choose a common basing and its preferred
zero-self-meridian longitudes. For every component $j$ and every finite
$q\geq2$, choose a lift $w_{j,q}\in F_r/\Gamma_qF_r$ of the class of its
longitude in $G/\Gamma_qG$, where $G=\pi_1(E_L)$ and $F_r$ is free on the
component meridian symbols. Such lifts exist because those meridians generate
every finite nilpotent quotient. For $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k,j)$, define the based
coefficient $\mu_L^b(I)$ by taking the coefficient of
$X_{i_1}\cdots X_{i_k}$ in $E(w_{j,k+1})$ through degree $k$. Let
$\Delta_I^b$ be the nonnegative greatest common divisor of the finite set of
all $\mu_L^b(J)$ for sequences $J$ of lengths from $2$ to $|I|-1$ that occur
as subsequences of cyclic permutations of $I$. The gcd of an empty set is $0$.
Define the based residue candidate
$$\bar\mu_L^b(I):=\mu_L^b(I)\pmod{\Delta_I^b}\in \mathbb Z/\Delta_I^b\mathbb Z,$$
with $\mathbb Z/0\mathbb Z=\mathbb Z$. Independence of the basing and word
lifts is not part of this definition; it is a separate theorem. A based
Borromean example with $I=(1,2,3)$ uses this convention.
thm-link-wirtinger-presentation-correctn:
## Statement

Assume countable choice.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a nonempty labeled link, after
inserting a small type-I curl on any component that has no underpassing point.
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be the positive meridians of the strands between
successive underpassing points, with the compatible common-upper-collar accesses of the local crossing rule. At a crossing $c$, write $o(c)$ for the
over-strand and $s(c),t(c)$ for the source and target under-sides defined using
the positive in-plane normal to the over-strand. Set
$$r_c=x_{o(c)}^{-1}x_{s(c)}x_{o(c)}x_{t(c)}^{-1}.$$
Then the assignment of each generator to its based positive meridian induces
an isomorphism
$$\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n\mid r_c\ (c\text{ a crossing})\rangle \cong \pi_1(E_L).$$
Any one crossing relator may be omitted without changing the represented
group. The theorem makes no claim that all relators are independent.

Arbitrary independently based positive strand meridians remain recorded: if $g_e$ is the access difference for strand $e$, its actual class is $y_e=g_ex_eg_e^{-1}$ in this reference presentation. This gives their exact group elements without claiming that the independently conjugated $y_e$ themselves freely generate the upper region or give the displayed uncorrected presentation. A common access change conjugates every generator and preserves the displayed presentation map.
alg-truncated-milnor-invariants-from-bas:
## Definition

Assume AC. The input is either (a) a based $r$-component string-link diagram
with its endpoint collars and product-tube parallels equal to the diagram's
blackboard push-offs, or (b) a based finite regular
diagram of a closed $r$-component labeled oriented link with chosen product
tubes, one initial strand on each component, and a common basepoint and access
paths. The finite input records its compatible common-upper-collar reference accesses. In the compatible branch the actual accesses are these, up to a common base-path change, and the parallels are the blackboard parallels already specified. In the arbitrary-choice branch it additionally records finite words in the compatible strand meridians for each access difference $g_e$, the parallel endpoint differences $h_{0,j},h_{1,j}$, and its relative meridian winding $k_j$. These are word certificates for the chosen paths, part of the supplied based-word data; no evaluation of an unencoded smooth path is claimed. In closed-link mode the preferred longitude uses its own recorded access $h_j$, which may differ from the initial-meridian access $g_j$. Arbitrary parallels are allowed in this branch, with the recorded $k_j$. The input also includes a maximum index length $N\geq2$. The output is
the integer coefficients $\mu_\tau(I)$ in string-link mode, or the based
coefficients $\mu_L^b(I)$, their lower indeterminacy data $\Delta_I^b$, and
residues $\bar\mu_L^b(I)$ in closed-link mode, for every index sequence $I$
with $2\leq |I|\leq N$.

Set $d=N-1$ and work in the truncated noncommutative ring
$$R_d=\mathbb Z\langle X_1,\ldots,X_r\rangle/\mathfrak m^{d+1},$$
where $\mathfrak m$ is the ideal generated by the letters. Carry out the
following finite procedure.

1. Verify the finite crossing, orientation, over/under, and component data. If
   a closed-link component has no underpassing point, insert a small type-I
   curl on that component in a disk meeting no other component and record the
   resulting based diagram. Give every strand $a$ the component label $j(a)$.

2. First compute in the compatible reference root symbols $x_j$, irrespective of the actual access choices. For every strand $a$, initialize its meridian series by
   $Y_a^{(1)}=1+X_{j(a)}$. For each degree $\ell=2,\ldots,d$, copy every
   $Y_a^{(\ell-1)}$ into the constant and lower-degree part of
   $Y_a^{(\ell)}$, with new degree-$\ell$ terms initially zero, and reset each
   chosen root strand to $1+X_j$. Then do one pass over each component in its
   oriented order. In closed-link mode start at the chosen initial strand and
   omit the final undercrossing back to that strand; in string-link mode start
   at the bottom endpoint and use every undercrossing through to the top
   endpoint. At an undercrossing with over-strand $o$ and source and target
   under-arcs $s,t$, use the already available $Y_o^{(\ell-1)}$ and the
   current $Y_s^{(\ell)}$ to set
   $$Y_t^{(\ell)}=\operatorname{trunc}_{\ell}\bigl((Y_o^{(\ell-1)})^{-1} Y_s^{(\ell)}Y_o^{(\ell-1)}\bigr)$$
   when the traversal is source-to-target, and set
   $$Y_s^{(\ell)}=\operatorname{trunc}_{\ell}\bigl(Y_o^{(\ell-1)} Y_t^{(\ell)}(Y_o^{(\ell-1)})^{-1}\bigr)$$
   when it is target-to-source. Here $\operatorname{trunc}_{\ell}$ discards
   monomials of degree greater than $\ell$, and every inverse is the finite
   geometric series in the nilpotent ideal of $R_d$.

3. For each component $j$, traverse its undercrossings in order and form
   $W_j=\prod_c (Y_{o(c)}^{(d)})^{\epsilon_c}$, where the factors are in
   traversal order and $\epsilon_c=+1$ for source-to-target and $-1$ for
   target-to-source. In string-link mode set $\Lambda_j=W_j$. In closed-link
   mode set
   $$\Lambda_j=(1+X_j)^{-\operatorname{wr}_j(D)}W_j,$$
   where $\operatorname{wr}_j(D)$ is the sum of the determinant signs at
   self-crossings of component $j$.

4. In the arbitrary-choice branch evaluate each supplied transport word by the strand series from step 2. Write $G_e$ for the resulting unit series, and $H_{0,j},H_{1,j}$ for the endpoint transport series. In string-link mode replace the compatible $\Lambda_j=W_j$ by
   $$H_{0,j}(1+X_j)^{k_j}W_jH_{1,j}^{-1}.$$
   In closed-link mode replace the compatible preferred series by
   $$H_j(1+X_j)^{-\operatorname{wr}_j(D)}W_jH_j^{-1},$$
   where $H_j=H_{0,j}=H_{1,j}$ is the actual longitude access difference, independently of the initial-meridian difference $G_j$. The arbitrary parallel winding cancels in the preferred correction. All powers and inverses are finite truncated operations. To express this result in the actual component-meridian symbols, form
   $$G_j(1+X_j)G_j^{-1}=1+X_j+R_j(X),\qquad \deg R_j\ge2.$$
   With new letters $V_j$, initialize $Z_j^{(1)}=V_j$ and iterate
   $$Z_j^{(s+1)}=\operatorname{trunc}_d\bigl(V_j-R_j(Z^{(s)})\bigr),\qquad 1\le s<d.$$
   Substitute $X_j=Z_j^{(d)}(V)$ in the corrected longitude series. This is its expansion in the chosen actual meridians. For the compatible branch this step is the identity. Rename the final letters $V_j$ as $X_j$.

5. For every $I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k,j)$ with $1\leq k\leq d$, read the coefficient
   of $X_{i_1}\cdots X_{i_k}$ in $\Lambda_j$. In string-link mode return this
   integer. In closed-link mode, also compute the gcd of the coefficients for
   all proper subsequences of cyclic permutations of $I$ of lengths at least
   two, with empty gcd equal to zero, and return the corresponding residue
   class.

All scans, including the supplied transport words and the $d-1$ inverse-substitution iterations, are over finite crossing, strand, degree, and index sets. The
procedure makes no polynomial-time claim. If a finite-input validation fails,
return `invalid-input`.
lem-link-nilpotent-peripheral-presentati:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let a nonempty labeled oriented closed link have a based regular diagram with an underpass on every component. Choose an initial arc on each component, its positive meridian $x_i$, and the common upper basing. Put $F=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_r\rangle$ and $G=\pi_1(E_L)$. For every $q\ge2$ there are explicit words $l_{i,q}\in F$ representing the preferred longitudes in $G/\Gamma_qG$ such that the meridian map identifies
$$G/\Gamma_qG\cong F/\langle\!\langle\Gamma_qF,[x_i,l_{i,q}]\ (1\le i\le r)\rangle\!\rangle.$$
The words can be chosen coherently through each finite degree. They are obtained through the $(q-1)$st approximation of the crossing-conjugation recursion, initialized by component meridians and using the preceding approximation for every over-arc. In particular this describes the kernel, rather than merely the surjectivity, of the component-meridian map. Quotienting further by commutators of arbitrary conjugates of each component meridian adds exactly those commutators to this presentation.
lem-milnor-basing-indeterminacy-and-self:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $L$ be a nonempty labeled oriented link in $S^3$, let
$I=(i_1,\ldots,i_k,j)$ have length at least two, and let $b,b'$ be any two
based meridian-longitude word systems used in the preceding definition. Then
the based residue candidates $\bar\mu_L^b(I)$ and $\bar\mu_L^{b'}(I)$ agree
under the canonical identification of their residue groups. If $L$ and $L'$ are
related by a finite sequence of self-crossing changes, the same residue is
preserved whenever the entries of $I$ are pairwise distinct. No invariance for
repeated-index sequences under self-crossing changes is asserted.
thm-truncated-milnor-computation-termina:
## Statement

Assume AC and let the based diagram, peripheral data, and maximum index length
$N\geq2$ satisfy the input conditions of the preceding algorithm. Put
$d=N-1$. The algorithm terminates after finitely many diagram, degree, and
monomial operations. In string-link mode, its output for each $I$ with
$2\leq|I|\leq N$ equals the integer coefficient of the based longitude in the
bottom-end quotient $F_r/\Gamma_{|I|}F_r$. In closed-link mode, its output
equals the based coefficient, gcd indeterminacy, and residue candidate defined
from the chosen peripheral word lifts. It makes no polynomial-time claim.
thm-milnor-invariants-isotopy-and-link-h:
## Statement

Assume AC. Every integer Milnor coefficient of a based string link is invariant
under smooth isotopy through string links fixing the endpoint collars. For
closed labeled oriented links, the residue candidate $\bar\mu_L(I)$ is invariant
under ambient isotopy. A link-homotopy is a finite sequence of ambient isotopies
and local crossing changes in which the two branches at every crossing change
belong to the same component. Under link-homotopy, $\bar\mu_L(I)$ is invariant
when the entries of $I$ are pairwise distinct. No invariance for repeated-index
sequences under link-homotopy is asserted.
